controls.label: Agent identity verification
controls.description: Can the counterparty verify which agent (software and operator) is acting?

controls.label: Agent registration (know your agent)
controls.description: Must the agent be registered, reviewed or listed before it can transact?

controls.label: User consent capture
controls.description: Is the user's authorization captured in a signed, inspectable artifact?

controls.label: Spending caps
controls.description: Can a maximum amount or budget be bound to the authorization?

controls.label: Merchant or payee scoping
controls.description: Can the authorization be limited to named merchants or payees?

controls.label: Time windows and expiry
controls.description: Do authorizations, tokens or signatures expire by design?

controls.label: Revocation
controls.description: Can the user or operator cancel an authorization before it is used?

controls.label: Step-up authentication
controls.description: Can the flow escalate to the human for a stronger check?

controls.label: Replay protection
controls.description: Are nonces, single-use proofs or time windows enforced against replay?

controls.label: Receipts and evidence
controls.description: Does the flow produce signed receipts or evidence usable later?

controls.label: Dispute support
controls.description: Are chargebacks, refunds or disputes part of the protocol?

controls.label: Reputation
controls.description: Is there a public or shared record of counterparty behavior?

controls.label: Monitoring signals
controls.description: What can a monitor observe to detect abuse while it happens?

controls.label: Kill switch
controls.description: Can an operator stop an agent's ability to transact at once?

cells.note: Identity is optional and separate from payment: sign-in-with-x (CAIP-122 wallet proof), auth-hints (OAuth 2.0 with DPoP) and RFC 9421 agent signatures in cloudflare:402.
No registry in x402. ERC-8004 can record that an agent accepts x402; cloudflare:402 needs the signature agent registered with Cloudflare.
The protocol has no consent object. The browser paywall asks a human in the UI; agents rely on mandates from other protocols such as AP2.
Budgets are out of scope in the spec. The TypeScript client applies spendControls by default (default assets only, $1 per payment); upto signs a ceiling.
The signature covers payTo and the amount; upto also names the one facilitator allowed to settle.
validAfter, validBefore, Permit2 deadline, maxTimeoutSeconds and Lightning invoice expiry bound every authorization.
A signed exact authorization cannot be recalled before it expires. auth-capture adds void and client reclaim after captureDeadline; batch-settlement channels allow timed withdrawal.
The specification defines no step-up or challenge beyond the 402 itself.
Single-use 32-byte nonces enforced by EIP-3009 tokens, Permit2 nonces, cumulative vouchers, and replay stores for Lightning payment hashes.
PAYMENT-RESPONSE carries the transaction hash; the optional offer-receipt extension signs offers and receipts (TypeScript only).
No dispute process. exact has no refund; auth-capture adds refunds, and third parties such as x402r add arbitration.
None in x402. ERC-8004 feedback can carry proofOfPayment for an x402 payment.
Settlements are public on chain but look like ordinary transfers; /supported, Bazaar and x402scan are public; header contents are private.
No protocol kill switch. Clients stop by policy or spendControls; servers stop by removing routes; facilitators can refuse to settle.
